intended_object: The evaluation homomorphism Γ(Y, O_Y) → L for an L-valued point p : Spec L → Y of a K-scheme Y, where L/K is a field extension. It sends a global section f to its value f(p) ∈ L, i.e. the pullback p^* : Γ(Y) → Γ(Spec L) composed with Γ(Spec L) ≅ L. Inferred from the docstring and from how the module uses it, through kernels of evaluations.
explanation:
The body is the map induced on global sections by `p.1.appTop : Γ(Y) ⟶ Γ(Spec L)`, followed by the canonical isomorphism `Scheme.ΓSpecIso L : Γ(Spec L) ≅ L`. That is exactly the standard way to evaluate global sections at an L-point. The ring homomorphism is the right one, and `eval_ker` confirms that its kernel is the kernel of `appTop`.

The construction only uses the underlying scheme morphism Spec L → Y. It would therefore make sense for any morphism Spec R → X with R a commutative ring. Mathlib, however, has no named "evaluation at an R-point" definition. The nearest is the Γ–Spec adjunction bijection, a different packaging. Here the notion is deliberately the evaluation at an L-valued point of a K-scheme, the setting in which the file states its density results for field-valued points. The bundled K-structure is simply what an L-point of a K-scheme is. So the definition matches its intended object at the generality the file uses, and I do not judge it too narrow.
